title: DocSign: the free, encrypted DocuSign alternative for crypto deal paperwork
content_html:
Every crypto team ends up signing the same kinds of documents: SAFTs, SAFEs, token warrants, advisor and vesting agreements, and SPV or fund subscription paperwork. Most reach for DocuSign, then hit the paywall as soon as they need more than a couple of envelopes a month. DocSign is a free, encrypted alternative for document signing, and it comes with your Cryptool account.

What DocSign is

DocSign is a digital document signing app, sometimes written doc sign or eSign, for teams that want legally sound e-signatures without a per-seat subscription. You upload a document, place signature and date fields, send it to signers, and collect a signed copy with a timestamped audit trail. Every document is encrypted in your browser before it reaches the server, so only you and your signers can read it.

Why not just use DocuSign

DocuSign is the best known name in eSign, but for a small crypto team it has real drawbacks:

  • The free tier is tiny, and real use pushes you onto a paid plan quickly.
  • Pricing is per seat, which adds up across founders, counsel, and operations.
  • Your signed agreements live in a third-party account you do not control.

DocSign covers the same core document signing, sending, e-signature, storage, and an audit trail, free with your Cryptool account, and adds client-side encryption built around crypto deal paperwork.

What you can do with DocSign

  • Upload a PDF or agreement and add signature, initial, and date fields.
  • Send it to one or many signers and track who has signed.
  • Get a signed copy with a clear, timestamped audit trail.
  • Keep every signed document next to your deals and investors in Cryptool.

Who it is for

Token projects issuing SAFTs and token warrants, funds and syndicates collecting SPV and subscription documents, and any crypto team that wants free, private digital document signing instead of another DocuSign bill.

Getting started

Open DocSign with your Cryptool account, upload your first document, add signers, and send it for signature in a couple of minutes. If you do not have an account yet, you can create one free.

Try it: https://cryptool.io/docsign
